title: Fuel and Throttle Component Locations — 5.2L
introduction:
I use this 5.2L reference to separate air control, fuel distribution and the location of the fuel pump driver module (FPDM). Each illustration has its own adjacent table, so match a callout within that view before moving to the next one.

In the engine view, the throttle body sits at the front of the intake. Its valve controls incoming air. The long fuel rails run along the engine banks, supplying the injectors positioned beneath them. An injector is an electrically controlled metering valve: the rail distributes fuel, while the injectors decide how much is delivered. It is the difference between a supply pipe and the taps it feeds.

The transparent engine rendering makes those relationships visible through surrounding parts; it does not mean the components are exposed for service. The separate vehicle view locates the FPDM assembly in the left-hand rear-seat area, with its precise position stated in the table. That is a location reference, not a seat-cushion removal instruction.

This page identifies components and their roles. It does not provide fuel-pressure tests, connector details or removal steps. Fuel rails can retain pressure after shutdown, so any later work that opens the fuel system needs the applicable pressure-release procedure first; engine-off alone is not confirmation that the rail is depressurized.

edits.why: This view locates the throttle body, injectors and fuel rails for the specified engine. Ti-VCT means twin independent variable camshaft timing; it identifies the engine configuration here rather than a fuel-system service step.
FPDM means fuel pump driver module. The separate body view locates its assembly beneath the rear seat cushion on the LH side, away from the engine-mounted components shown above.
